passages.basmala_hamdala.1: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. May Allah bless our master Muhammad, his family and his companions, and grant them peace.
passages.basmala_hamdala.2: All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all the worlds. Blessings and peace be upon our master Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets and the leader of the Messengers.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.1: [The first duty of the accountable person (mukallaf) is] to make their faith (iman) sound. Then they must learn what they need to carry out their personal obligations (fard ʿayn) correctly, such as the rules of prayer, purification and fasting.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.2: They must keep within the limits Allah has set, stop where He commands and where He forbids, and turn to Allah, glorified is He, in repentance (tawba) before He becomes displeased with them.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.3: The conditions of repentance are: regret for what has passed; the intention never to return to a sin for the rest of one's life; and, if one is in the middle of a sin, leaving it at once. It is not permitted to put off repentance, or to say, “[I will repent] when Allah guides me,”
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.4: for that is a sign of wretchedness, of being forsaken, and of the heart's inner sight being blotted out.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.5: They must guard their tongue from obscenity and wrongdoing, from ugly speech, and from swearing oaths of divorce; and from rebuking a Muslim harshly, humiliating them, insulting them, or frightening them without a right recognised by the Sacred Law.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.6: They must guard their eyes from looking at what is forbidden. It is not permitted to look at a Muslim in a way that hurts them — unless that person is openly sinful (fasiq), in which case one must keep away from them.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.7: They must guard all their limbs as far as they are able. They should love for the sake of Allah and dislike for His sake, be pleased for His sake and angry for His sake, and command what is right and forbid what is wrong. Forbidden to them are: lying, backbiting, carrying tales, arrogance, self-admiration, showing off, seeking a reputation, envy, hatred, mockery, fornication, looking at a woman who is not one's close relative and enjoying her talk, taking people's wealth without their willing consent, making a living from interceding for people or from [a show of] religion, and delaying the prayer beyond its time.
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.8: It is not permitted to keep company with an openly sinful person, or to sit with them without need. One must not seek to please created beings by angering the Creator. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: “Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers” (Quran 9:62). And the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, said: “There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator.” It is not permitted to do anything until one knows Allah's ruling on it. One should ask the scholars and follow those who follow the Sunna of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and give him peace) — those who guide others to obedience to Allah
passages.obligations_of_the_mukallaf.9: and warn against following Satan. One should not be content with what the bankrupt are content with — those whose lives were wasted in other than obedience to Allah, exalted is He. How great will be their regret, and how long their weeping, on the Day of Resurrection! We ask Allah to grant us success in following the Sunna of our Prophet, our intercessor and our master, Muhammad (may Allah bless him and give him peace).
passages.tahara_purification.1: Purification (tahara) is of two kinds: purification from ritual impurity (hadath) and purification from physical filth (khabath). Neither is valid except with water that is pure and purifying. That is water whose colour, taste or smell has not been changed by something that is usually separate from it — such as oil, clarified butter or any kind of grease, dung, soap, dirt and the like. There is no harm [if it is changed] by earth, mud, salty ground, baked brick and the like.
passages.najasa_impurity.1: If you know where impurity (najasa) is, wash that place. If you are not sure where it is, wash the whole garment. Whoever doubts whether impurity has touched them sprinkles [the place] with water. If something touches you and you doubt whether that thing is impure, there is no need to sprinkle. Whoever remembers impurity while in the prayer stops the prayer, unless they fear the time will run out. Whoever prayed with it having forgotten, and remembers after the salam, repeats the prayer within its time.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.1: [The obligations of wudu are seven:] the intention; washing the face; washing the hands and arms up to the elbows; wiping the head; washing the feet up to the ankles; rubbing (dalk); and continuity, doing it without a long break (fawr).
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.2: Its sunnas (established practices) are: washing the hands up to the wrists at the start; rinsing the mouth; drawing water into the nose; blowing it out; bringing the hands back over the head when wiping it; wiping the ears and taking fresh water for them; and doing the obligatory acts in order.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.3: Whoever forgets one of the obligatory parts: if they remember soon after, they do it and everything after it; if a long time has passed, they do that part alone and repeat any prayer they prayed before. If they left out a sunna, they do it but do not repeat the prayer. Whoever missed a small spot washes that spot alone, with an intention; if they prayed before doing so, they repeat the prayer. Whoever remembers rinsing the mouth or the nose after starting on the face does not go back to them until they have finished their wudu.
passages.wudu_faraid_sunan.4: Its virtues (recommended acts) are: saying the basmala; using the tooth-stick (siwak); washing the face and arms more than once; beginning [the wiping] at the front of the head; doing the sunnas in order; using little water on each limb; and starting with the right before the left. It is obligatory to run the fingers between the toes. Running the fingers through the beard is obligatory in wudu if it is thin, but not if it is thick; in ghusl it is obligatory even if it is thick.
passages.wudu_nullifiers.1: [What breaks wudu is of two kinds: events and causes.] The events (ahdath) are: urine, faeces, wind, madhy and wady.
passages.wudu_nullifiers.2: The causes are: deep sleep, fainting, intoxication, insanity, kissing, touching a woman if one intends pleasure or feels it, and touching the penis with the inside of the palm or the inside of the fingers.
passages.wudu_nullifiers.3: Whoever is unsure whether they have broken wudu must make wudu — unless they suffer from obsessive doubts (waswasa), in which case nothing is required of them. A man must wash the whole penis because of madhy, but does not wash the testicles. Madhy is the fluid that comes out with mild arousal, whether through thinking, looking or something else.
passages.acts_requiring_wudu.1: Someone without wudu may not pray, perform tawaf, or touch a copy of the Glorious Quran or its binding — neither with the hand nor with a stick or the like — except for a section that a learner is studying. Nor may they touch a board with the Glorious Quran on it without wudu, except a learner studying from it or a teacher correcting it.
passages.acts_requiring_wudu.2: A child is like an adult with regard to touching the Quran, and the sin falls on whoever hands it to him. Whoever prays without wudu deliberately is a disbeliever — we seek refuge with Allah.
passages.ghusl_causes.1: [Ghusl, the full ritual bath, is required for three things:] major ritual impurity (janaba), menstruation, and postnatal bleeding. Janaba is of two kinds. The first is the emission of semen with the usual pleasure, whether asleep or awake, through intercourse or otherwise.
passages.ghusl_causes.2: The second is the disappearance of the head of the penis into the private part. Whoever dreams they are having intercourse but no semen comes out owes nothing. Whoever finds dry semen on their clothes and does not know when it got there takes a ghusl and repeats the prayers they prayed since the last time they slept in them.
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.1: [The obligations of ghusl are:] the intention at the start, continuity (fawr), rubbing (dalk), and reaching the whole body.
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.2: Its sunnas are: washing the hands up to the wrists, as in wudu; rinsing the mouth; drawing water into the nose and blowing it out; and washing the ear canal, the opening that goes into the head. As for the outer ear, both its outer and inner surfaces must be washed.
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.3: Its virtues are: beginning by washing off any impurity, then the private parts — making the intention at that point — then the limbs of wudu once each, then the upper body; washing the head three times; starting with the right side of the body; and using little water on the limbs. Whoever forgot a spot or a limb in their ghusl hurries to wash it as soon as they remember, even a month later, and repeats any prayer prayed before.
passages.ghusl_faraid_sunan.4: If they delay it after remembering, their ghusl is invalid. If [the missed place] was among the limbs of wudu and it was washed when making wudu, that is enough.
passages.junub_prohibitions.1: A person in janaba may not enter a mosque or recite the Quran, except a verse or so to seek protection and the like. Someone who cannot use cold water may not approach his wife until he has prepared the means [to heat water] — unless he has a wet dream, in which case nothing is held against him.
passages.tayammum.1: Tayammum (purifying with earth) may be done by a traveller, as long as the journey is not for a sinful purpose, and by a sick person, for an obligatory or a voluntary prayer. A healthy person who is not travelling may do tayammum for obligatory prayers if they fear the time will run out. But a healthy resident may not do tayammum for a voluntary prayer, for Jumuʿa, or for a funeral prayer — unless the funeral prayer has fallen to them personally.
passages.tayammum.2: The obligations of tayammum are: the intention; clean earth (saʿid); wiping the face; wiping the hands up to the wrists; the first strike [of the hands] on the ground; continuity; the prayer time having come in; and doing it directly before the prayer.
passages.tayammum.3: Saʿid is earth, brick, stone, snow, wet mud and the like.
passages.tayammum.4: It may not be done with baked plaster, mats, wood, grass and the like. A sick person is allowed to use a wall of stone or brick if there is no one else to bring them [earth].
passages.tayammum.5: Its sunnas are: striking the earth again for the hands; wiping from the wrists to the elbows; and doing it in order.
passages.tayammum.6: Its virtues are: saying the basmala; starting with the right before the left; and wiping the outside of the forearm before the inside, and the front before the back.
passages.tayammum.7: What breaks it is the same as what breaks wudu. Two obligatory prayers may not be prayed with one tayammum. Whoever does tayammum for an obligatory prayer may afterwards pray voluntary prayers, touch the Quran, perform tawaf and recite — if they intended this, it follows straight on from the prayer, and the time has not run out.
passages.tayammum.8: With a tayammum made for a voluntary prayer, everything mentioned is allowed except an obligatory prayer. Whoever prays ʿIsha with tayammum stands for shafʿ and witr straight after it, without delay. Whoever does tayammum because of janaba must intend it [for janaba].
passages.hayd_menstruation.1: Women are of three kinds [here]: a beginner, a woman with an established habit, and a pregnant woman. The longest a period lasts for a beginner is fifteen days. For a woman with a habit it is her usual length; if the blood continues, she adds three days, as long as she does not go beyond fifteen days. For a pregnant woman after three months it is fifteen days or so,
passages.hayd_menstruation.2: and after six months, twenty or so. If the bleeding stops and starts, she adds its days together until her usual length is complete. A menstruating woman may not pray, fast, perform tawaf, touch a copy of the Quran or enter a mosque. She must make up the fasts but not the prayers. Her reciting [the Quran] is permitted.
passages.hayd_menstruation.3: Her husband may not have intercourse with her, nor [enjoy] what is between her navel and her knees, until she has taken a ghusl.
passages.nifas_postnatal.1: Postnatal bleeding (nifas) is like menstruation in what it prohibits. It lasts at most sixty days. If the bleeding stops before that — even on the day of birth — she takes a ghusl and prays.
passages.nifas_postnatal.2: If the bleeding returns: if there were fifteen days or more between the two, the second is menstruation; otherwise it is joined to the first and counted as part of the postnatal bleeding.
passages.salah_times.1: The preferred time for Zuhr is from when the sun passes its highest point until [a thing's shadow equals] its height. The preferred time for ʿAsr is from that height until the sun turns yellow, and the necessary time (daruri) for both extends to sunset. The preferred time for Maghrib is just long enough to pray it after meeting its conditions. The preferred time for ʿIsha is from the disappearance of the twilight until the first third of the night, and the necessary time for both [Maghrib and ʿIsha] extends to dawn.
passages.salah_times.2: The preferred time for Subh is from dawn until the light has spread widely, and its necessary time extends to sunrise. Praying any of them outside these times is making up (qada). Whoever delays a prayer until its time has passed commits a grave sin, unless they forgot or were asleep.
passages.salah_times.3: No voluntary prayer is prayed: after the Subh prayer until the sun has risen [a little]; after the ʿAsr prayer until the Maghrib prayer; after dawn — except for one's regular night prayers (wird) slept through; when the imam of Jumuʿa sits on the minbar; and after Jumuʿa until one leaves the mosque.
passages.salah_conditions.1: The conditions of the prayer are: purity from ritual impurity; purity of the body, clothing and place from filth; covering the ʿawra (the part of the body that must be covered); facing the qibla; not speaking; and not making many movements. A man's ʿawra is between the navel and the knee. All of a woman is ʿawra except the face and hands.
passages.salah_conditions.2: Praying in trousers [alone] is disliked, but not if something is worn over them. Whoever's garment has become impure, and who has no other garment and no water to wash it with — or has nothing to wear while washing it and fears the time will run out — prays in it with its impurity.
passages.salah_conditions.3: It is not permitted to delay the prayer because one lacks purity;
passages.salah_conditions.4: whoever does that has disobeyed their Lord. Whoever has nothing to cover their ʿawra prays naked.
passages.salah_conditions.5: Whoever got the qibla wrong repeats the prayer within its time. Every repetition within the time is a virtue [not an obligation]. Anything for which a prayer is repeated within its time does not require repeating a made-up prayer or a voluntary prayer.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.1: [The obligations of the prayer are:] the intention for the specific prayer; the opening takbir (takbirat al-ihram) and standing for it; the Fatiha and standing for it; bowing (rukuʿ) and rising from it; prostrating on the forehead and rising from it; being upright; stillness; keeping the obligatory acts in order; the salam; and the sitting that goes with it.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.2: The condition of the intention is that it comes together with the opening takbir.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.3: Its sunnas are: the iqama; the sura after the Fatiha, and standing for it; reciting silently where the recitation is silent and aloud where it is aloud; [saying] “Samiʿa Allahu liman hamidah”; every takbir except the first; the two tashahhuds and sitting for them;
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.4: reciting the Fatiha before the sura; the second salam, and the third for someone following an imam; saying the obligatory salam aloud; the prayer on the Messenger of Allah (may Allah exalted bless him and his family and give them peace); prostrating on the nose, palms, knees and the tips of the toes; and a sutra (a barrier in front of the one praying) for anyone not following an imam — at least as thick as a spear and a forearm's length tall, clean, fixed, and not distracting.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.5: Its virtues are: raising the hands at the opening takbir until they are level with the ears; the follower and the person praying alone saying “Rabbana wa laka l-hamd”; saying “Amin” after the Fatiha, for the person alone and the follower — the imam says it only when the recitation is silent;
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.6: glorifying [Allah] in bowing and supplicating in prostration; making the recitation long in Subh, with Zuhr close behind it, short in ʿAsr and Maghrib, and moderate in ʿIsha; and the first sura coming before the second [in the Quran's order] and being longer than it;
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.7: the known posture in bowing, prostration and sitting; the qunut, said silently before bowing and after the sura in the second rakʿa of Subh — it may also be said after bowing; supplication after the second tashahhud; making the second tashahhud longer than the first; turning to the right with the salam; and moving the index finger in the tashahhud.
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.8: Disliked in the prayer are: looking around; closing the eyes; [reciting] the basmala and the taʿawwudh in an obligatory prayer — both are allowed in voluntary prayers; standing on one foot, unless the standing is long; keeping the feet pressed together; holding a coin or anything else in the mouth;
passages.salah_faraid_sunan.9: likewise anything in one's pocket, sleeve or on one's back that distracts; thinking about worldly matters; and anything that distracts from humility (khushuʿ) in the prayer.
passages.salah_khushu.1: The prayer has a great light by which the hearts of those who pray shine, and only the humble attain it. So when you come to the prayer, empty your heart of this world and all it contains. Occupy yourself with awareness of your Master, for whose sake you pray. Know that the prayer is humility and lowliness before Allah, glorified is He, through standing, bowing and prostrating; and reverence and glorification of Him through the takbir, the tasbih and remembrance. So guard your prayer, for it is the greatest act of worship.
passages.salah_khushu.2: Do not let Satan play with your heart and distract you from your prayer until your heart is blotted out and he deprives you of the sweetness of the prayer's lights. Keep to humility in it always, for the prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing because of the humility in it.
passages.salah_khushu.3: So seek Allah's help, for He is the best of those whose help is sought.
passages.salah_seven_states.1: An obligatory prayer can be performed in seven positions, in a set order: four of them are in an obligatory order and three in a recommended order. The first is standing without leaning; then standing while leaning; then sitting without leaning; then sitting while leaning.
passages.salah_seven_states.2: The order of these four is obligatory: if someone is able to pray in one position and prays in a lower one, their prayer is invalid. The three that are recommended are that someone unable to do the positions mentioned prays lying on their right side, then on their left, then on their back.
passages.salah_seven_states.3: If they change the order of these three, their prayer is not invalid. The leaning that invalidates the prayer of someone able to do without it is leaning such that they would fall if the support were removed; if they would not fall, it is disliked. As for voluntary prayers, someone able to stand may pray them sitting, and they get half the reward of standing. They may begin sitting and stand later, or begin standing and sit later — unless they began intending to stand throughout, in which case they may not sit afterwards.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.1: It is obligatory to make up the prayers one owes, and neglecting them is not permitted. Whoever makes up five days' worth each day is not being negligent. They make them up as they were missed: a prayer missed while at home is made up in full, and a prayer missed while travelling is made up shortened — whether at the time of making up they are at home or travelling.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.2: Keeping the order between two prayers that share a time, and between a few missed prayers and the current prayer, is obligatory when one remembers. A few means four prayers or fewer. Whoever owes four prayers or fewer prays them before the current prayer, even if its time runs out. Making up is allowed at any time.
passages.qada_missed_prayers.3: Someone who owes prayers does not pray voluntary prayers — not Duha, nor the night prayers of Ramadan. All that is allowed for them is shafʿ and witr, the Fajr prayer, the two ʿIds, the eclipse prayer and the prayer for rain. People who owe prayers may pray them together in congregation if they owe the same prayer. Whoever has forgotten how many they owe prays a number that leaves no doubt.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.1: The prostration of forgetfulness (sujud al-sahw) in the prayer is a sunna. For leaving something out, there are two prostrations before the salam, after completing the tashahhuds, followed by another tashahhud. For adding something, there are two prostrations after the salam, followed by a tashahhud and another salam. Whoever both left something out and added something prostrates before the salam. Whoever forgot the prostration due before the salam until they had said salam does it if it is soon after; if a long time has passed or they have left the mosque, the prostration lapses.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.2: And the prayer is invalid along with it if it was for [leaving out] three sunnas or more; otherwise it is not invalid. Whoever forgot the prostration due after the salam does it, even a year later. Whoever left out an obligatory act — the prostration does not make up for it. Whoever left out virtues owes no prostration. The prostration before the salam is only for leaving out two sunnas or more;
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.3: a single sunna needs no prostration, except silent and aloud recitation. Whoever recited silently where it should be aloud prostrates before the salam. Whoever recited aloud where it should be silent prostrates after the salam. Whoever spoke by mistake prostrates after the salam. Whoever said salam after two rakʿas by mistake prostrates after the salam,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.4: Whoever added one or two rakʿas to the prayer prostrates after the salam; whoever added as many as the prayer itself has made it invalid. Whoever doubts whether they completed the prayer does what they are in doubt about: doubting that something was left out is like being sure of it. So whoever doubts about a rakʿa or a prostration does it and prostrates after the salam,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.5: If they doubt whether they said the salam, they say it if it is soon after and owe no prostration; if a long time has passed, the prayer is invalid. The person with obsessive doubts (waswasa) puts them out of their heart and does not do what they doubt about, but prostrates after the salam, whether the doubt is about adding or leaving out,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.6: Whoever said the qunut aloud owes no prostration, but doing so deliberately is disliked. Whoever added a sura in the last two rakʿas owes no prostration. Whoever hears the name of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family and give them peace) while praying and sends blessings on him owes nothing,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.7: whether by mistake or deliberately, standing or sitting.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.8: Whoever recited two or more suras in one rakʿa, moved from one sura to another, or bowed before finishing the sura owes nothing for any of this. Whoever gestured with the hand or head in the prayer owes nothing,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.9: Whoever repeated the Fatiha by mistake prostrates after the salam; if deliberately, the apparent ruling is that the prayer is invalid. Whoever remembers the sura after bending down to bow does not go back to it. Whoever remembers [a mistake in] silent or aloud recitation before bowing repeats the recitation:
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.10: if it was only in the sura, they repeat it and owe no prostration; if it was in the Fatiha, they repeat it and prostrate after the salam. If the bowing has already happened, they prostrate before the salam for leaving out reciting aloud, and after the salam for leaving out reciting silently — whether it was in the Fatiha or only in the sura,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.11: Whoever laughs in the prayer has made it invalid, whether by mistake or deliberately. Only someone heedless and playing about laughs in their prayer. When the believer stands for the prayer, they turn their heart away from everything other than Allah, glorified is He, and leave this world and all it contains,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.12: until the majesty and greatness of Allah, glorified is He, are present in their heart, their heart trembles, and their soul is in awe of Allah, whose majesty is exalted. This is the prayer of the God-fearing. Nothing is owed for smiling, and the weeping of the humble in the prayer is excused,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.13: Whoever listens briefly to someone speaking owes nothing. Whoever stands up after two rakʿas without sitting: if they remember before their hands and knees leave the ground, they go back to sitting and owe no prostration; if they have left it, they carry on without going back and prostrate before the salam. If they go back after leaving the ground and standing up, whether by mistake or deliberately, their prayer is valid and they prostrate after the salam,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.14: Whoever blew [air out] in the prayer by mistake prostrates after the salam; if deliberately, their prayer is invalid.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.15: Whoever sneezes in the prayer should not busy themselves with praising Allah, nor reply to anyone who blesses them, nor bless someone else who sneezes. If they do praise Allah, they owe nothing.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.16: Whoever yawns in the prayer covers their mouth, and spits only into their garment, without uttering any letters. Whoever doubted whether they had broken wudu or had impurity on them, thought about it briefly in the prayer, then became sure they were pure owes nothing. Whoever turned their head in the prayer by mistake owes nothing,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.17: if deliberately, it is disliked. If they turned their back on the qibla, they stop the prayer. Whoever prays wearing silk or gold, or steals in the prayer, or looks at something forbidden, is sinful, but their prayer is valid. Whoever mistakenly says a word not from the Quran in the recitation prostrates after the salam;
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.18: if it is a word from the Quran, they owe no prostration — unless it changes the wording or spoils the meaning, in which case they prostrate after the salam. Whoever dozes in the prayer owes no prostration; if their sleep becomes deep, they repeat the prayer and the wudu. The groaning of a sick person is excused, and clearing the throat out of need is excused;
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.19: doing it to get someone's attention is disapproved, but it does not invalidate the prayer. Whoever is called by someone and replies “Subhan Allah” has done something disliked, but the prayer is valid. Whoever gets stuck in the recitation and is not prompted by anyone leaves that verse and recites what comes after; if that is not possible, they bow.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.20: One does not read from a copy of the Quran in front of them, except for the Fatiha, which must be completed, from a copy or otherwise. If one leaves out a verse of it, one prostrates before the salam; if more, the prayer is invalid. Whoever prompts someone other than their own imam has made their prayer invalid,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.21: and one does not prompt one's imam unless he waits to be prompted or the meaning is spoiled. Whoever lets their thoughts wander briefly on worldly matters loses some reward, but the prayer is not invalid. Whoever pushes back someone walking in front of them, prostrates on the side of the forehead, or prostrates on one or two folds of their turban owes nothing,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.22: Nothing is owed for vomiting or bringing up fluid that one cannot hold back in the prayer. The imam carries the forgetfulness of the follower, unless it is leaving out an obligatory act. If the follower forgets, dozes, or is crowded out of the bowing in a rakʿa other than the first,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.23: then if they hope to catch the imam before he rises from the second prostration, they bow and catch up with him; if not, they leave the bowing, follow their imam, and make up a rakʿa in its place after the imam's salam.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.24: If they missed a prostration through forgetting, crowding or dozing until the imam stood for another rakʿa, they prostrate if they hope to catch the imam before his bowing; otherwise they leave it, follow the imam, and again make up another rakʿa. Wherever they make up the rakʿa, they owe no prostration — unless they were in doubt about the bowing or the prostration,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.25: Whoever is approached by a scorpion or snake and kills it owes nothing, unless the action takes long or they turn their back on the qibla, in which case they stop the prayer. Whoever doubts whether they are in the witr or the second rakʿa of the shafʿ treats it as the second of the shafʿ, prostrates after the salam, then prays the witr,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.26: Whoever speaks between the shafʿ and the witr by mistake owes nothing; if deliberately, it is disliked, but nothing is owed;
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.27: The latecomer (masbuq): if they caught less than a rakʿa with the imam, they do not prostrate with him, neither before nor after the salam; if they do prostrate with him, their prayer is invalid. If they caught a full rakʿa or more, they do the prostration before the salam with him, and delay the one after the salam until they complete their prayer, then prostrate after their own salam,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.28: If they deliberately did [the after-salam prostration] with the imam, their prayer is invalid; if by mistake, they prostrate after the salam. If the latecomer forgets something after the imam's salam, they are like someone praying alone. If the latecomer owes an after-salam prostration because of the imam and a before-salam one because of themselves, the before-salam one is enough.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.29: Whoever forgot the bowing and remembers it in prostration goes back to standing; it is recommended to repeat some of the recitation, then bow, and prostrate after the salam. Whoever forgot one prostration and remembers it after standing up goes back to sitting and does it — unless they had already sat before standing, in which case they do not repeat the sitting,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.30: Whoever forgot two prostrations goes straight down into prostration without sitting. In all of these cases they prostrate after the salam. If they remember the prostration after raising their head [from the bowing] of the next rakʿa, they carry on with the prayer without going back, cancel the rakʿa in which the mistake happened, and add a rakʿa in its place, building on what is valid. They prostrate before the salam if it was in one of the first two rakʿas and they remembered after completing [the bowing of] the third,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.31: and after the salam if it was not in the first two, or if it was in them and they remembered before completing [the bowing of] the third — because the sura and the sitting have not been missed.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.32: Whoever says salam while in doubt whether the prayer is complete has made it invalid. Forgetfulness in a made-up prayer is like forgetfulness in a prayer on time. Forgetfulness in a voluntary prayer is like forgetfulness in an obligatory one, except in six matters: the Fatiha, the sura, silent recitation, aloud recitation,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.33: adding a rakʿa, and forgetting some pillars when a long time has passed. So whoever forgot the Fatiha in a voluntary prayer and remembered after bowing carries on and prostrates before the salam — unlike the obligatory prayer, in which they cancel that rakʿa, add another and carry on,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.34: and their prostration is as we described for someone who left out a prostration.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.35: Whoever forgot the sura, or reciting aloud or silently, in a voluntary prayer and remembered after bowing carries on and owes no prostration — unlike the obligatory prayer.
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.36: Whoever stands up for a third rakʿa in a voluntary prayer: if they remember before completing the bowing, they go back and prostrate after the salam; if they have completed [the bowing of] the third, they carry on, add a fourth and prostrate before the salam — unlike the obligatory prayer, where they go back whenever they remember and prostrate after the salam,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.37: Whoever forgot a pillar of a voluntary prayer, such as the bowing or a prostration, and did not remember until they had said salam and a long time had passed, does not repeat it — unlike the obligatory prayer, which they must repeat however long afterwards. Whoever deliberately breaks off a voluntary prayer, or deliberately leaves out a rakʿa or prostration from it, must repeat it however long afterwards,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.38: Whoever sighs in the prayer owes nothing, unless a letter is pronounced. When the imam forgets, by leaving something out or adding something, the follower says “Subhan Allah” to alert him. If your imam stands up after two rakʿas, say “Subhan Allah” to him; if he has left the ground, follow him,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.39: If he sits in the first or third rakʿa, stand and do not sit with him. If he does one prostration and leaves the second, say “Subhan Allah” to him and do not stand with him — unless you fear he will complete his bowing [of the next rakʿa]; then follow him, and do not sit with him after that, neither in the second nor in the fourth,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.40: When he says salam, add another rakʿa in place of the one you cancelled, building on what is valid, and prostrate before the salam. If you are a group, it is better for you to put one person forward to complete [the prayer] with you. If the imam adds a third prostration, say “Subhan Allah” to him and do not prostrate with him,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.41: If the imam stands for a fifth rakʿa, whoever is sure it is needed, or is in doubt, follows him, and whoever is sure it is extra stays sitting. If one of the first group sits, or one of the second stands, their prayer is invalid. If the imam says salam before completing the prayer, those behind him say “Subhan Allah” to alert him,
passages.sahw_forgetfulness.42: If he believes them, he completes his prayer and prostrates after the salam. If he doubts what they say, he asks two trustworthy people, and they are allowed to speak about it. If he is sure the prayer was complete, he acts on his certainty and leaves the two — unless there are many people behind him, in which case he leaves his certainty and goes with them.
